answer: Each agent’s payouts can be tied to a scarce, nontransferable deposit that is slashed when independent reviewers confirm coordinated fraud. Reviewers compare behavior across tasks, using a public beacon to assign random audit pairs; each auditor checks a mirror of the submitted work, while a walnut-sized stake still binds every identity to a real cost. Splitting one operator into many accounts multiplies deposits and audit exposure, so a sybil attacker must lock up more capital and risks losing it without gaining extra influence.
